transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: Hi Jordan, welcome! Today we want to dive into your experience with distributed event architectures, React Server Components, and live transcript streaming.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Vance
transcript.text: Thanks Alex! At my previous role, I designed our real-time collaboration pipeline using WebSocket pub/sub backed by Redis and optimistic state reconciliation on the client.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Brody
transcript.text: How did you handle network partition recovery and state resynchronization when a client drops for 30 seconds?

transcript.speaker: Jordan Vance
transcript.text: We attached monotonically increasing sequence IDs to every delta chunk. On reconnect, the client sends its last known sequence ID and the server streams the missing delta buffer.

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: That matches our exact pattern. What is your preferred approach for managing local AI model keys and sensitive customer JWTs?

transcript.speaker: Jordan Vance
transcript.text: HTTP-only secure SameSite cookies for server sessions, with client BYOK keys isolated to in-memory state or encrypted localStorage with explicit user consent.
